name: Belmond Hotel das Cataratas
positioning: Pink Portuguese colonial-style hotel inside Iguacu National Park, beside Iguassu Falls (officially Hotel das Cataratas, A Belmond Hotel)
best_for: Travelers who want to see the falls with extra time inside the park
Nature lovers who want guided wildlife walks and a garden setting

facts.text: The hotel is located inside the Iguassu park, which gives guests up to six additional hours to explore beyond the park's 9-5 opening hours for other visitors.
The hotel building dates from 1958 and is a Portuguese colonial-style building in delicate pink.
The hotel's lawns slope down to a lookout over Iguacu Falls.
The hotel has a colonial tower that rises above the trees.
Floors are dark wood and bathrooms are finished in white marble.
The hotel has an infinity pool.
The gardens are planted with orchids and bromeliads.
The spa sources its treatment ingredients from the surrounding jungle.
The bar serves a Devil's Throat cocktail, named after the horseshoe waterfall.
Ipe restaurant serves Brazilian barbecue from a grill run by a gaucho chef.
A hotel guide offers bio-tours of the park's fauna.
Activities include helicopter and boat tours.

highlights.text: Staying inside the park gives guests up to six additional hours to explore beyond the 9-5 hours for other visitors.
The hotel's lawns slope down to a lookout over Iguacu Falls.
A colonial tower rises above the trees, and the hotel has a pink facade.
The spa sources its treatment ingredients from the surrounding jungle.
Ipe restaurant serves Brazilian barbecue from a grill run by a gaucho chef.

considerations.text: There are no other buildings for miles around the hotel.
WhataHotel notes the remote location within the national park limits dining and entertainment options.
